rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a well-balanced multimodal configuration with strong components. This experiment tests a multimodal model using scgpt (advanced RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (high-performing image encoder), transformer aggregation (flexible feature combination), and concat fusion (standard approach). It clarifies the baseline performance of key components, providing a reference point for future experiments.

The existing evidence shows that the current best (config_005) uses scgpt RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. This experiment tests changing the fusion method to 'weighted' while keeping other components the same, which could clarify if fusion strategy significantly impacts performance. It balances exploitation (building on a promising multimodal setup) and exploration (testing a key hyperparameter variation).

Existing evidence shows config_010 (weighted fusion) outperforms config_005 (concat fusion) by ~0.013 accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from transformer to avgpool while keeping weighted fusion (same as config_010) improves performance. It clarifies if aggregation method is a key factor, balancing exploitation of current best practices with exploration of alternative design choices.

The existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion yield the highest accuracy (0.542) so far. This experiment tests whether switching the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion unchanged) could improve performance. It clarifies the impact of image encoder choice on accuracy, a key design choice with uncertain optimal value.

The existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion yield the highest accuracy (0.542) so far. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (vs. scgpt and imagenet_vit_l in config_018) with the same aggregation/fusion could improve performance, clarifying if encoder choices are critical. It balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of alternative encoders, prioritizing high-impact design choices.

The existing evidence shows config_030 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 and switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer, which could reveal if these changes improve performance. It balances exploration (testing new image encoder) and exploitation (using pca_n2000 RNA encoder) while addressing uncertainty about image encoder impact.

Existing evidence shows pca_n2000 RNA encoder (config_030) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests combining pca_n2000 RNA with resnet50 image encoder (from config_017) but uses transformer aggregation and concat fusion instead of avgpool/weighted. This clarifies whether changing aggregation/fusion methods can further improve performance while maintaining the effective RNA encoder. It balances exploitation of pca_n2000's strength with exploration of alternative modal interaction strategies.

The existing evidence shows config_030 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). However, uncertainty remains about whether using transformer aggregation and concat fusion (as in config_001) could further improve performance. This experiment tests a key design choice (aggregation/fusion method) that hasn't been explored with these encoders, balancing exploitation of current top performers with exploration of alternative architectures.

The existing evidence shows config_030 (pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted) has the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders but with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion, clarifying if fusion type impacts performance. It balances exploitation (focusing on top-performing components) and exploration (testing a key design choice variation) to maximize chances of finding the optimal configuration within the remaining experiment.
